summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, recent CABG and mitral valve replacement, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for leg swelling and weight gain due to decompensated diastolic heart failure. She had a history of urinary retention requiring a catheter and was on bethanechol, which contributed to diarrhea. Hyperkalemia and hyponatremia on admission resolved with diuresis. A scheduled left lower extremity angiogram was postponed due to kidney concerns. She improved with IV lasix, weight decreased, and electrolytes normalized. Coccygeal pain from a recent fall was managed with acetaminophen. She was discharged home with instructions to hold torsemide and warfarin before the rescheduled vascular procedure and to monitor daily weights.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Closed fracture of sacrum and coccyx without mention of spinal cord injury
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
